Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit

- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T03:10:19Z

## PR Description

Closes #1713

Covers BOTH parts of the card: the flutter_app sandbox cluster (threshold restored 74.13 → 30.0) and the round-2 CORE ratchet (root threshold restored 90.0 → 12.0, the gh-1234 line). README CRAP badges synced back; `scripts/check_crap_guards.py` green (badge sync + exclude parity).

## Per-method CC (hand-computed, McCabe: base 1 + each if/for/while/case/`||`/`&&`/`??`/ternary)

CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)³ + CC (the 0.14.2 formula, verified against the card's measured table).

| Method | Before (CC @ cov → CRAP) | After (CC → est CRAP) | Treatment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MemoryShell._runCommand` | 74 @ 97% → 74.13 | **3** → ~3.0 | Static `_commandRoutes` route table (`shell`, `ctx` closures), one entry per advertised command — aliases (`[`/`test`, `python`/`python3`, `xz`/`unxz`, `gzip`/`gunzip`, `pip`/`pip3`, `qjs`/`js`) and the `_hashCommands` family get their own entries; dispatch = guard-if + null-check + call. `_buildCommandRoutes` helper: CC 2. |
| `WasiSandboxShell._runBuiltin` | 43 @ 93% → 43.59 | **2** → ~2.0 | Same treatment: static `_builtinRoutes` table of `(s, st, o, src)` closures; every original per-builtin call signature preserved (that per-entry variance is why the table is data, not a switch); unknown-builtin fallback kept. |
| `detectLanguage` | 39 @ 100% → 39.0 | **3** → 3.0 | `_extensionLanguages` extension-map data table (37 keys, no dot, lowercased — byte-identical mapping incl. the `''`-ext and unknown-ext → `plaintext` paths). |
| `_connectionDisplayName` | 12 @ 42% → 40.58 | **5** → ~9.9 | Preset display-name switch extracted to `_presetDisplayNames` data table + `_presetDisplayName` (CC 2, `?? preset.name` fallback). Custom-row and `toString` arms unchanged. |
| `MemoryShell._interpretEchoEscapes` | 11 @ 43% → 33.58 | **3** → 3.0 | `_echoEscapes` data table + `_echoEscapeAt` seam (CC 3). Now covered by a new `echo -e` test (all five table arms + unknown-escape passthrough + trailing backslash) in `test/memory_shell_test.dart`. |
| `WasmSshCommands.builtinsFor` | 6 @ 0% → 42.0 | **6** → 6.0 @ 100% cov | CC already ≤ 30 once covered — the 0% cov was the whole CRAP story. New `test/wasm_shell_ssh_builtins_test.dart` drives all five local closures (read/write/kind/list/mkdir incl. parent-creation, sorted listing, missing → null) against a temp sandbox host dir; no SSH involved. |
| **core** `_typeName` | 9 @ 0% → 90.00 | **9** → 9.0 @ 100% cov | Pure name-table, CC already minimal — coverage was the problem. New `type naming in parse errors` group in `test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart` drives all seven arms (nothing/string/number int+double/boolean/object/array/runtimeType) through the public `parseProviderQueueEntries` error paths. |
| **core** `BindingProvenance.label` | 8 @ 25% → 35.00 | **1** → 1.0 | The switch duplicated the enum name arm for arm (all seven labels == `.name`). Getter is now `=> name` — CC 1, CRAP coverage-independent (≤ 2 at 0% cov). |

## Core-ratchet scoping note (round 2 addendum)

Both core offenders from the 2026-10-19 addendum are addressed in this PR — no scoping out: `_typeName` (90.00) and `BindingProvenance.label` (35.00) were the only core entries above the 12.0 line per the card's local reproduction on the merged core shards, so the root `crap4dart.yaml` threshold is restored 90.0 → 12.0 in the same commit train, with the badge synced and the `raise-issue: gh-1713` / Restored comment trail following the gh-992 precedent.

## Gates (run in the lane worktree on a standalone toolchain)

- `dart analyze` (standalone SDK) on `lib/src/model_roles` + `test/model_roles`: clean.
- `flutter analyze` on the four touched app lib files: zero findings from this diff (two `empty_catches` infos are pre-existing gh-925 guards, untouched; plus package-level flutter_inappwebview plugin-declaration noise).
- `dart test` `providers_queue_test.dart` + `provider_model_binding_test.dart`: **105 passed** (incl. the new type-naming group).
- `flutter test` on the touched app suites (memory_shell, wasm_shell pipeline/host-cwd/builtins/stat/ssh-builtins/modules, sandbox parity/job-log/conformance, provider_connection_guard): **473 passed** (incl. the new echo -e, display-name and ssh-builtin tests). Two compile bugs the analyzer gate alone did not surface (wildcarded closure params referenced in the body) were caught by exactly these runs and fixed before commit.
- `dart format` clean on every touched file.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/wasm_shell.dart` stays under the 2800 loc gate: **2797**.
- `scripts/check_crap_guards.py`: ✅ (badge sync, exclude parity).

Note on CRAP numbers: the local agent cube cannot produce the lcov inputs (flutter coverage collector EPERMs through `.worktrees` — known, documented in `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`), so the after-CRAP column is computed from the formula at expected coverage, not locally re-measured. The CI app-crap-gate / core CRAP gates are the arbiter for both restored thresholds; suites above prove the behavior is unchanged so the coverage inputs should reproduce.

## Round 2 (CI validation): the four core offenders CI lcov surfaced

Run 39679365314 measured four functions above the restored 12.0 core line that the card's table did not list. All four descended on this branch (f9570fed31); threshold stays 12.0.

| `_cellRange` (timeline_projection.dart:314) | 14 @ 57.1% → 29.43 | **4** → 4.0 @ 100% | Start/duration lookups split into `_recordStart` (CC 7) + `_recordDurationMs` (CC 5); all arms covered by three new timed-mode tests (every anchored kind incl. compacted/system, unanchored/context drop, negative + missing duration clamps). |

Per-family options preserved byte-for-byte. |
| `_defaultRoleStyle` (tui_theme.dart:646) | 21 @ 100% → 21.00 | **1** → 1.0 | The 20-arm role-name switch is now the `_defaultRoleStyles` data-table lookup (identity values, `null` default via absent keys). |

Run 39692028722's core CRAP census (pulled from the job log) shows the card's round-2 table was only the tip: **42 methods measure > 12.0** under CI lcov — the fully-covered CC-13…21 dispatcher tier (which 0.14.2 counts higher than the CC-12 tier gh-1234 documented under 0.11) plus a 0%-cov CC-4 tier. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …
Let me start by reading the input context files as instructed.
{"path":"input"}

- **Title**: refactor(1713): descend CRAP ratchets to 30.0 (app) / 12.0 (core) under crap4dart 0.14.2
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `refactor/1713-crap-descent` → `main`
- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T03:10:19Z

## PR Description

Closes #1713

Covers BOTH parts of the card: the flutter_app sandbox cluster (threshold restored 74.13 → 30.0) and the round-2 CORE ratchet (root threshold restored 90.0 → 12.0, the gh-1234 line). README CRAP badges synced back; `scripts/check_crap_guards.py` green (badge sync + exclude parity).

## Per-method CC (hand-computed, McCabe: base 1 + each if/for/while/case/`||`/`&&`/`??`/ternary)

CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)³ + CC (the 0.14.2 formula, verified against the card's measured table).

| Method | Before (CC @ cov → CRAP) | After (CC → est CRAP) | Treatment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MemoryShell._runCommand` | 74 @ 97% → 74.13 | **3** → ~3.0 | Static `_commandRoutes` route table (`shell`, `ctx` closures), one entry per advertised command — aliases (`[`/`test`, `python`/`python3`, `xz`/`unxz`, `gzip`/`gunzip`, `pip`/`pip3`, `qjs`/`js`) and the `_hashCommands` family get their own entries; dispatch = guard-if + null-check + call. `_buildCommandRoutes` helper: CC 2. |
| `WasiSandboxShell._runBuiltin` | 43 @ 93% → 43.59 | **2** → ~2.0 | Same treatment: static `_builtinRoutes` table of `(s, st, o, src)` closures; every original per-builtin call signature preserved (that per-entry variance is why the table is data, not a switch); unknown-builtin fallback kept. |
| `detectLanguage` | 39 @ 100% → 39.0 | **3** → 3.0 | `_extensionLanguages` extension-map data table (37 keys, no dot, lowercased — byte-identical mapping incl. the `''`-ext and unknown-ext → `plaintext` paths). |
| `_connectionDisplayName` | 12 @ 42% → 40.58 | **5** → ~9.9 | Preset display-name switch extracted to `_presetDisplayNames` data table + `_presetDisplayName` (CC 2, `?? preset.name` fallback). Custom-row and `toString` arms unchanged. |
| `MemoryShell._interpretEchoEscapes` | 11 @ 43% → 33.58 | **3** → 3.0 | `_echoEscapes` data table + `_echoEscapeAt` seam (CC 3). Now covered by a new `echo -e` test (all five table arms + unknown-escape passthrough + trailing backslash) in `test/memory_shell_test.dart`. |
| `WasmSshCommands.builtinsFor` | 6 @ 0% → 42.0 | **6** → 6.0 @ 100% cov | CC already ≤ 30 once covered — the 0% cov was the whole CRAP story. New `test/wasm_shell_ssh_builtins_test.dart` drives all five local closures (read/write/kind/list/mkdir incl. parent-creation, sorted listing, missing → null) against a temp sandbox host dir; no SSH involved. |
| **core** `_typeName` | 9 @ 0% → 90.00 | **9** → 9.0 @ 100% cov | Pure name-table, CC already minimal — coverage was the problem. New `type naming in parse errors` group in `test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart` drives all seven arms (nothing/string/number int+double/boolean/object/array/runtimeType) through the public `parseProviderQueueEntries` error paths. |
| **core** `BindingProvenance.label` | 8 @ 25% → 35.00 | **1** → 1.0 | The switch duplicated the enum name arm for arm (all seven labels == `.name`). Getter is now `=> name` — CC 1, CRAP coverage-independent (≤ 2 at 0% cov). |

## Core-ratchet scoping note (round 2 addendum)

Both core offenders from the 2026-10-19 addendum are addressed in this PR — no scoping out: `_typeName` (90.00) and `BindingProvenance.label` (35.00) were the only core entries above the 12.0 line per the card's local reproduction on the merged core shards, so the root `crap4dart.yaml` threshold is restored 90.0 → 12.0 in the same commit train, with the badge synced and the `raise-issue: gh-1713` / Restored comment trail following the gh-992 precedent.

## Gates (run in the lane worktree on a standalone toolchain)

- `dart analyze` (standalone SDK) on `lib/src/model_roles` + `test/model_roles`: clean.
- `flutter analyze` on the four touched app lib files: zero findings from this diff (two `empty_catches` infos are pre-existing gh-925 guards, untouched; plus package-level flutter_inappwebview plugin-declaration noise).
- `dart test` `providers_queue_test.dart` + `provider_model_binding_test.dart`: **105 passed** (incl. the new type-naming group).
- `flutter test` on the touched app suites (memory_shell, wasm_shell pipeline/host-cwd/builtins/stat/ssh-builtins/modules, sandbox parity/job-log/conformance, provider_connection_guard): **473 passed** (incl. the new echo -e, display-name and ssh-builtin tests). Two compile bugs the analyzer gate alone did not surface (wildcarded closure params referenced in the body) were caught by exactly these runs and fixed before commit.
- `dart format` clean on every touched file.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/wasm_shell.dart` stays under the 2800 loc gate: **2797**.
- `scripts/check_crap_guards.py`: ✅ (badge sync, exclude parity).

Note on CRAP numbers: the local agent cube cannot produce the lcov inputs (flutter coverage collector EPERMs through `.worktrees` — known, documented in `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`), so the after-CRAP column is computed from the formula at expected coverage, not locally re-measured. The CI app-crap-gate / core CRAP gates are the arbiter for both restored thresholds; suites above prove the behavior is unchanged so the coverage inputs should reproduce.

## Round 2 (CI validation): the four core offenders CI lcov surfaced

Run 39679365314 measured four functions above the restored 12.0 core line that the card's table did not list. All four descended on this branch (f9570fed31); threshold stays 12.0.

| Method | Before (CC @ cov → CRAP) | After (CC → est CRAP) | Treatment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `_cellRange` (timeline_projection.dart:314) | 14 @ 57.1% → 29.43 | **4** → 4.0 @ 100% | Start/duration lookups split into `_recordStart` (CC 7) + `_recordDurationMs` (CC 5); all arms covered by three new timed-mode tests (every anchored kind incl. compacted/system, unanchored/context drop, negative + missing duration clamps). |

| `_CatalogStreamFunction.call` (provider_catalog.dart:799) | ~9 @ ~40% → 26.13 | **4** → ≤ 7.5 worst case | The structural one: adapter dispatch is now a `_builders` route table (kind → builder); the four OpenAI-compatible kinds share one builder; the five family builders each keep CC 1, so their coverage no longer matters (≤ 2 CRAP each). Per-family options preserved byte-for-byte. |
| `_defaultRoleStyle` (tui_theme.dart:646) | 21 @ 100% → 21.00 | **1** → 1.0 | The 20-arm role-name switch is now the `_defaultRoleStyles` data-table lookup (identity values, `null` default via absent keys). |

Shared-checkout hygiene: an initial mis-pathed edit batch landed in the shared checkout and was reverted to HEAD before reapplication (checkout verified clean, `git status` empty).


## Round 3 (CI recurrence on a6109ac8): the full 0.14.2 tier — 42 methods

Run 39692028722's core CRAP census (pulled from the job log) shows the card's round-2 table was only the tip: **42 methods measure > 12.0** under CI lcov — the fully-covered CC-13…21 dispatcher tier (which 0.14.2 counts higher than the CC-12 tier gh-1234 documented under 0.11) plus a 0%-cov CC-4 tier. Both core offenders from the 2026-10-19 addendum are addressed in this PR — no scoping out: `_typeName` (90.00) and `BindingProvenance.label` (35.00) were the only core entries above the 12.0 line per the card's local reproduction on the merged core shards, so the root `crap4dart.yaml` threshold is restored 90.0 → 12.0 in the same commit train, with the badge synced and the `raise-issue: gh-1713` / Restored comment trail following the gh-992 precedent.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. - **Title**: refactor(1713): descend CRAP ratchets to 30.0 (app) / 12.0 (core) under crap4dart 0.14.2
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `refactor/1713-crap-descent` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 53
- **Additions**: +2851
- **Deletions**: -1640
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T21:18:06Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T03:10:19Z

## PR Description

Closes #1713

Covers BOTH parts of the card: the flutter_app sandbox cluster (threshold restored 74.13 → 30.0) and the round-2 CORE ratchet (root threshold restored 90.0 → 12.0, the gh-1234 line). README CRAP badges synced back; `scripts/check_crap_guards.py` green (badge sync + exclude parity).

## Per-method CC (hand-computed, McCabe: base 1 + each if/for/while/case/`||`/`&&`/`??`/ternary)

CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)³ + CC (the 0.14.2 formula, verified against the card's measured table).

| Method | Before (CC @ cov → CRAP) | After (CC → est CRAP) | Treatment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MemoryShell._runCommand` | 74 @ 97% → 74.13 | **3** → ~3.0 | Static `_commandRoutes` route table (`shell`, `ctx` closures), one entry per advertised command — aliases (`[`/`test`, `python`/`python3`, `xz`/`unxz`, `gzip`/`gunzip`, `pip`/`pip3`, `qjs`/`js`) and the `_hashCommands` family get their own entries; dispatch = guard-if + null-check + call. `_buildCommandRoutes` helper: CC 2. |
| `WasiSandboxShell._runBuiltin` | 43 @ 93% → 43.59 | **2** → ~2.0 | Same treatment: static `_builtinRoutes` table of `(s, st, o, src)` closures; every original per-builtin call signature preserved (that per-entry variance is why the table is data, not a switch); unknown-builtin fallback kept. |
| `detectLanguage` | 39 @ 100% → 39.0 | **3** → 3.0 | `_extensionLanguages` extension-map data table (37 keys, no dot, lowercased — byte-identical mapping incl. the `''`-ext and unknown-ext → `plaintext` paths). |
| `_connectionDisplayName` | 12 @ 42% → 40.58 | **5** → ~9.9 | Preset display-name switch extracted to `_presetDisplayNames` data table + `_presetDisplayName` (CC 2, `?? preset.name` fallback). Custom-row and `toString` arms unchanged. |
| `MemoryShell._interpretEchoEscapes` | 11 @ 43% → 33.58 | **3** → 3.0 | `_echoEscapes` data table + `_echoEscapeAt` seam (CC 3). Now covered by a new `echo -e` test (all five table arms + unknown-escape passthrough + trailing backslash) in `test/memory_shell_test.dart`. |
| `WasmSshCommands.builtinsFor` | 6 @ 0% → 42.0 | **6** → 6.0 @ 100% cov | CC already ≤ 30 once covered — the 0% cov was the whole CRAP story. New `test/wasm_shell_ssh_builtins_test.dart` drives all five local closures (read/write/kind/list/mkdir incl. parent-creation, sorted listing, missing → null) against a temp sandbox host dir; no SSH involved. |
| **core** `_typeName` | 9 @ 0% → 90.00 | **9** → 9.0 @ 100% cov | Pure name-table, CC already minimal — coverage was the problem. New `type naming in parse errors` group in `test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart` drives all seven arms (nothing/string/number int+double/boolean/object/array/runtimeType) through the public `parseProviderQueueEntries` error paths. |
| **core** `BindingProvenance.label` | 8 @ 25% → 35.00 | **1** → 1.0 | The switch duplicated the enum name arm for arm (all seven labels == `.name`). Getter is now `=> name` — CC 1, CRAP coverage-independent (≤ 2 at 0% cov). |

## Core-ratchet scoping note (round 2 addendum)

Both core offenders from the 2026-10-19 addendum are addressed in this PR — no scoping out: `_typeName` (90.00) and `BindingProvenance.label` (35.00) were the only core entries above the 12.0 line per the card's local reproduction on the merged core shards, so the root `crap4dart.yaml` threshold is restored 90.0 → 12.0 in the same commit train, with the badge synced and the `raise-issue: gh-1713` / Restored comment trail following the gh-992 precedent.

## Gates (run in the lane worktree on a standalone toolchain)

- `dart analyze` (standalone SDK) on `lib/src/model_roles` + `test/model_roles`: clean.
- `flutter analyze` on the four touched app lib files: zero findings from this diff (two `empty_catches` infos are pre-existing gh-925 guards, untouched; plus package-level flutter_inappwebview plugin-declaration noise).
- `dart test` `providers_queue_test.dart` + `provider_model_binding_test.dart`: **105 passed** (incl. the new type-naming group).
- `flutter test` on the touched app suites (memory_shell, wasm_shell pipeline/host-cwd/builtins/stat/ssh-builtins/modules, sandbox parity/job-log/conformance, provider_connection_guard): **473 passed** (incl. the new echo -e, display-name and ssh-builtin tests). Two compile bugs the analyzer gate alone did not surface (wildcarded closure params referenced in the body) were caught by exactly these runs and fixed before commit.
- `dart format` clean on every touched file.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/wasm_shell.dart` stays under the 2800 loc gate: **2797**.
- `scripts/check_crap_guards.py`: ✅ (badge sync, exclude parity).

Note on CRAP numbers: the local agent cube cannot produce the lcov inputs (flutter coverage collector EPERMs through `.worktrees` — known, documented in `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`), so the after-CRAP column is computed from the formula at expected coverage, not locally re-measured. The CI app-crap-gate / core CRAP gates are the arbiter for both restored thresholds; suites above prove the behavior is unchanged so the coverage inputs should reproduce.

## Round 2 (CI validation): the four core offenders CI lcov surfaced

Run 39679365314 measured four functions above the restored 12.0 core line that the card's table did not list. All four descended on this branch (f9570fed31); threshold stays 12.0.

| Method | Before (CC @ cov → CRAP) | After (CC → est CRAP) | Treatment |

| `_cellRange` (timeline_projection.dart:314) | 14 @ 57.1% → 29.43 | **4** → 4.0 @ 100% | Start/duration lookups split into `_recordStart` (CC 7) + `_recordDurationMs` (CC 5); all arms covered by three new timed-mode tests (every anchored kind incl. compacted/system, unanchored/context drop, negative + missing duration clamps). |

Per-family options preserved byte-for-byte. |

Run 39692028722's core CRAP census (pulled from the job log) shows the card's round-2 table was only the tip: **42 methods measure > 12.0** under CI lcov — the fully-covered CC-13…21 dispatcher tier (which 0.14.2 counts higher than the CC-12 tier gh-1234 documented under 0.11) plus a 0%-cov CC-4 tier. ## Description

Closes #1713

## Per-method CC (hand-computed, McCabe: base 1 + each if/for/while/case/`||`/`&&`/`??`/ternary)

CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)³ + CC (the 0.14.2 formula, verified against the card's measured table).

| Method | Before (CC @ cov → CRAP) | After (CC → est CRAP) | Treatment |

| `MemoryShell._runCommand` | 74 @ 97% → 74.13 | **3** → ~3.0 | Static `_commandRoutes` route table (`shell`, `ctx` closures), one entry per advertised command — aliases (`[`/`test`, `python`/`python3`, `xz`/`unxz`, `gzip`/`gunzip`, `pip`/`pip3`, `qjs`/`js`) and the `_hashCommands` family get their own entries; dispatch = guard-if + null-check + call. `_buildCommandRoutes` helper: CC 2. |
| `WasiSandboxShell._runBuiltin` | 43 @ 93% → 43.59 | **2** → ~2.0 | Same treatment: static `_builtinRoutes` table of `(s, st, o, src)` closures; every original per-builtin call signature preserved (that per-entry variance is why the table is data, not a switch); unknown-builtin fallback kept. |
| `detectLanguage` | 39 @ 100% → 39.0 | **3** → 3.0 | `_extensionLanguages` extension-map data table (37 keys, no dot, lowercased — byte-identical mapping incl. the `''`-ext and unknown-ext → `plaintext` paths). |
| `_connectionDisplayName` | 12 @ 42% → 40.58 | **5** → ~9.9 | Preset display-name switch extracted to `_presetDisplayNames` data table + `_presetDisplayName` (CC 2, `?? preset.name` fallback). Custom-row and `toString` arms unchanged. |
| `MemoryShell._interpretEchoEscapes` | 11 @ 43% → 33.58 | **3** → 3.0 | `_echoEscapes` data table + `_echoEscapeAt` seam (CC 3). Now covered by a new `echo -e` test (all five table arms + unknown-escape passthrough + trailing backslash) in `test/memory_shell_test.dart`. |
| `WasmSshCommands.builtinsFor` | 6 @ 0% → 42.0 | **6** → 6.0 @ 100% cov | CC already ≤ 30 once covered — the 0% cov was the whole CRAP story. | **core** `_typeName` | 9 @ 0% → 90.00 | **9** → 9.0 @ 100% cov | Pure name-table, CC already minimal — coverage was the problem. New `type naming in parse errors` group in `test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart` drives all seven arms (nothing/string/number int+double/boolean/object/array/runtimeType) through the public `parseProviderQueueEntries` error paths. |

## Core-ratchet scoping note (round 2 addendum)

Both core offenders from the 2026-10-19 addendum are addressed in this PR — no scoping out: `_typeName` (90.00) and `BindingProvenance.label` (35.00) were the only core entries above the 12.0 line per the card's local reproduction on the merged core shards, so the root `crap4dart.yaml` threshold is restored 90.0 → 12.0 in the same commit train, with the badge synced and the `raise-issue: gh-1713` / Restored comment trail following the gh-992 precedent.

- `dart test` `providers_queue_test.dart` + `provider_model_binding_test.dart`: **105 passed** (incl. the new type-naming group).

Two compile bugs the analyzer gate alone did not surface (wildcarded closure params referenced in the body) were caught by exactly these runs and fixed before commit.

2143 AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). ## PR Description

Closes #1713

Covers BOTH parts of the card: the flutter_app sandbox cluster (threshold restored 74.13 → 30.0) and the round-2 CORE ratchet (root threshold restored 90.0 → 12.0, the gh-1234 line). README CRAP badges synced back; `scripts/check_crap_guards.py` green (badge sync + exclude parity).

## Per-method CC (hand-computed, McCabe: base 1 + each if/for/while/case/`||`/`&&`/`??`/ternary)

CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)³ + CC (the 0.14.2 formula, verified against the card's measured table).

| Method | Before (CC @ cov → CRAP) | After (CC → est CRAP) | Treatment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MemoryShell._runCommand` | 74 @ 97% → 74.13 | **3** → ~3.0 | Static `_commandRoutes` route table (`shell`, `ctx` closures), one entry per advertised command — aliases (`[`/`test`, `python`/`python3`, `xz`/`unxz`, `gzip`/`gunzip`, `pip`/`pip3`, `qjs`/`js`) and the `_hashCommands` family get their own entries; dispatch = guard-if + null-check + call. `_buildCommandRoutes` helper: CC 2. |
| `WasiSandboxShell._runBuiltin` | 43 @ 93% → 43.59 | **2** → ~2.0 | Same treatment: static `_builtinRoutes` table of `(s, st, o, src)` closures; every original per-builtin call signature preserved (that per-entry variance is why the table is data, not a switch); unknown-builtin fallback kept. |
| `detectLanguage` | 39 @ 100% → 39.0 | **3** → 3.0 | `_extensionLanguages` extension-map data table (37 keys, no dot, lowercased — byte-identical mapping incl. the `''`-ext and unknown-ext → `plaintext` paths). |
| `_connectionDisplayName` | 12 @ 42% → 40.58 | **5** → ~9.9 | Preset display-name switch extracted to `_presetDisplayNames` data table + `_presetDisplayName` (CC 2, `?? preset.name` fallback). Custom-row and `toString` arms unchanged. |
| `MemoryShell._interpretEchoEscapes` | 11 @ 43% → 33.58 | **3** → 3.0 | `_echoEscapes` data table + `_echoEscapeAt` seam (CC 3). Now covered by a new `echo -e` test (all five table arms + unknown-escape passthrough + trailing backslash) in `test/memory_shell_test.dart`. |
| `WasmSshCommands.builtinsFor` | 6 @ 0% → 42.0 | **6** → 6.0 @ 100% cov | CC already ≤ 30 once covered — the 0% cov was the whole CRAP story. New `test/wasm_shell_ssh_builtins_test.dart` drives all five local closures (read/write/kind/list/mkdir incl. parent-creation, sorted listing, missing → null) against a temp sandbox host dir; no SSH involved. |
| **core** `_typeName` | 9 @ 0% → 90.00 | **9** → 9.0 @ 100% cov | Pure name-table, CC already minimal — coverage was the problem. New `type naming in parse errors` group in `test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart` drives all seven arms (nothing/string/number int+double/boolean/object/array/runtimeType) through the public `parseProviderQueueEntries` error paths. |

## Core-ratchet scoping note (round 2 addendum)

Both core offenders from the 2026-10-19 addendum are addressed in this PR — no scoping out: `_typeName` (90.00) and `BindingProvenance.label` (35.00) were the only core entries above the 12.0 line per the card's local reproduction on the merged core shards, so the root `crap4dart.yaml` threshold is restored 90.0 → 12.0 in the same commit train, with the badge synced and the `raise-issue: gh-1713` / Restored comment trail following the gh-992 precedent.

## Gates (run in the lane worktree on a standalone toolchain)

- `dart analyze` (standalone SDK) on `lib/src/model_roles` + `test/model_roles`: clean.
- `flutter analyze` on the four touched app lib files: zero findings from this diff (two `empty_catches` infos are pre-existing gh-925 guards, untouched; plus package-level flutter_inappwebview plugin-declaration noise).
- `dart test` `providers_queue_test.dart` + `provider_model_binding_test.dart`: **105 passed** (incl. the new type-naming group).
- `flutter test` on the touched app suites (memory_shell, wasm_shell pipeline/host-cwd/builtins/stat/ssh-builtins/modules, sandbox parity/job-log/conformance, provider_connection_guard): **473 passed** (incl. the new echo -e, display-name and ssh-builtin tests). Two compile bugs the analyzer gate alone did not surface (wildcarded closure params referenced in the body) were caught by exactly these runs and fixed before commit.
- `dart format` clean on every touched file.
- `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/wasm_shell.dart` stays under the 2800 loc gate: **2797**.
- `scripts/check_crap_guards.py`: ✅ (badge sync, exclude parity).

Note on CRAP numbers: the local agent cube cannot produce the lcov inputs (flutter coverage collector EPERMs through `.worktrees` — known, documented in `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`), so the after-CRAP column is computed from the formula at expected coverage, not locally re-measured. The CI app-crap-gate / core CRAP gates are the arbiter for both restored thresholds; suites above prove the behavior is unchanged so the coverage inputs should reproduce.

Run 39679365314 measured four functions above the restored 12.0 core line that the card's table did not list. All four descended on this branch (f9570fed31); threshold stays 12.0.

Per-family options preserved byte-for-byte. |

Closes #1713

New `type naming in parse errors` group in `test/model_roles/providers_queue_test.dart` drives all seven arms (nothing/string/number int+double/boolean/object/array/runtimeType) through the public `parseProviderQueueEntries` error paths. |

Both core offenders from the 2026-10-19 addendum are addressed in this PR — no scoping out: `_typeName` (90.00) and `BindingProvenance.label` (35.00) were the only core entries above the 12.0 line per the card's local reproduction on the merged core shards, so the root `crap4dart.yaml` threshold is restored 90.0 → 12.0 in the same commit train, with the badge synced and the `raise-issue: gh-1713` / Restored comment trail following the gh-992 precedent.

2143 AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
